_comment: The single source of truth for where every array lives, before and after.
All numbers are hex strings so they can be compared against a disassembler
without arithmetic. Offsets are relative to the edit block unless the name
says otherwise; 'va' fields are absolute virtual addresses (this exe has no
ASLR: DllCharacteristics 0x8120, so a VA is also the runtime address).
Everything here is verified in docs/findings.md, 'Raising the caps'.
'base_new' is filled in by tools/patchset.py, packed after the old block end.

upper_belt._comment: Everything between the coach array's end and the 596-byte match table: the dummy triple, the four counts, upper1, the fixture table, upper2. The -upper sets move all of it by one delta to the grown block end so the player array can run up to the season calendar at 0x16038a8 (the old match-table region below it is dead once rec596 is relocated). The offsets here stay as the fingerprint the attribution walk keys on.
upper_belt._ceiling_note: the season calendar (stride 0x2c4) begins here; the shipped match table's last record runs into it, which is why rec596 has an extra end-pointer site

block.tail_pad_why: spare room after the relocated arrays, holding nothing. Some references to a relocated array are virtualised into .impdata, where the attribution cannot see them, and still compute from the old base; one such read was measured on 2026-09-17 at block + 0x3060284 and killed the season twice. The pad makes such a read land inside our own allocation. Reads only.

players.cap_note: 65000 was the aspiration; 33314 is what is actually reachable. The player array begins at offset 0 and cannot be relocated, so it can only grow into whatever sits above it, and what sits above it is the team array at 0xadf4bc and then the regulation array at 0xc12e9c. With the teams relocated out of the way the player array may run up to the regulation base and no further: 0xc12e9c / 0x17c is 33314 records, 36 bytes to spare. Passing that needs the regulations relocated too, and 306 of their sites are still unattributed.
players.note: starts at +0, so accesses carry no displacement; must grow in place, shifting everything above it

extra_cap_sites.why: block constructor 0x1414b8700: __ehvec_ctor(block, 0x17c, 30001, ctor 0x140a9fd00) -- the player array starts at offset 0, so the constructor takes the block pointer straight from rcx and the call names no array; the attribution walk had nothing to file it against. The matching destructor count at 0x1414ba61f was found by the copy scan and has been raised all along, so with the cap raised and this site left at 30001 the block constructed 30001 players and the destructor ran the player destructor over all 46193: 16192 records that were never constructed were destroyed as if they were, freeing whatever the allocator had left in their pointer fields.

block destructor: __ehvec_dtor of the same records. The copy scan already supplies this one for the sets that carry the mode-copy player patches, but a set that raises the player cap without them left it at 30001 while the constructor built cap_new -- the same asymmetry the other way round. Listed here so every set that raises the cap moves both ends.

The BACK EDGE of the team walk in 0x1412fb360, which indexes the array with `imul rcx, rax, 0x690` / `add rcx, 0xadf4bc` and builds an index keyed by the id in each record. The compiler peeled the first iteration: the guard at 0x1412fb41a tests r12d, which is zeroed before the loop and never changes, and every later pass enters at 0x1412fb42c and skips that guard entirely -- so this back edge is the only real bound the walk has. Raising the guard alone left the walk covering clubs 0..749 of 1600. Found 2026-09-16 by the back-edge sweep that check_cap_completeness now runs, after the same shape in the fixture array (0x141579e64) turned out to be the whole of G2a's remaining defect.

hold_sites.why: not a team bound at all, despite the 750. The loop in 0x140b10944 walks a table at block+0x16705a8 of 0x10-byte entries whose live count is the dword at block+0x1673488 -- and 0x16705a8 + 750*0x10 is exactly 0x1673488, so the table ends where its own counter begins. `cmp edi, 0x2ee` is the table's own size, and over it the code falls back to entry 0 rather than reading past the end. Raising it would write entries over the count. The table is count-driven, not indexed by team row, so the earlier reading of it as a per-team side table that cannot grow was wrong on both halves: it is not per-team, and the 750 is the structure, not a check.

B -> block: the loop bound over the copy's coach array, which holds 750 (0x1a1800 - 0x133a30 = 750 x 0x258), not 1300
A -> block (0x1414016b0): the loop bound over the copy's 750-record team array

The dummy-select sites next to them (cmp then a forward jb to the dummy record) may be raised: they only decide whether a block row past the old cap is real.

fixtures.note: Measured 2026-09-16: the 2000 records are GLOBAL -- one table for the whole world, not per season and not per competition. A record holds 16 match slots of 32 bytes at +4 with the count at +0x204, and one competition round takes one record per group. Two separate jobs now: G2a raises this cap, G2b widens the record to 32 slots (stride 0x408) so a single 36-club league phase fits. See docs/g2b-fixture-record.md. MEASURED AGAIN 2026-09-16 on a running 39-league season: all 2000 records are IN USE, shared by 56 competitions, and the table has already OVERFLOWED -- competition 143 starts at record 1997 and gets three rounds of sixteen before the array ends. A record is one ROUND of one competition: u32 competition at +0, 16 slots of 32 (home +0, away +4, match index +8, 0xffff +0xa, competition +0xc, round key +0xe, four 0x07f7ffff fillers at +0x10), and the number of slots the round uses in the low byte of +0x204. Suggested cap 6000. Note that copy B holds only 1750, so records 1750-1999 are already being dropped.

The BACK EDGE of the free-record search in 0x141579db0: `lea rdi, [rsi + 0xd65f64]` / `imul rcx, rax, 0x208`, walking the block's fixture array for a record whose head is 0xffff. Its ENTRY test at 0x141579e2e is the site the attribution walk found, because that one sits next to the array access; this one sits after the loop body and the walk never reached it. Found 2026-09-16 and it is the whole of G2a's remaining defect: with the entry test at 6000 and the back edge at 2000 the search still only ever examined records 0..1999, so once those were full the allocator reported no free record and the season stopped at exactly 2000 -- with every other bound in all 13 fixture functions verified live at 6000. Raised with the block cap.

extra_sites.why: lea rax, [rax*8 + 0xe63de4] in 0x140c4f0f0, whose rbx is the edit block ([owner+0x48], loaded through 0x1414b6a60 two instructions in). The block base arrives in a separate `add rax, rbx` after the lea, so the lea on its own shows no block reference and the attribution walk never filed it. It is the base of a 30000-entry 8-byte table inside upper2, searched linearly (cmp ecx, 0x7530) and then dereferenced (mov rax, [rax]); left behind by the belt move it would search the middle of the player array and dereference a player field as a pointer. The 0x7530 bound is deliberately not raised: the table cannot grow without room after it, so players past 30000 simply are not in it.

copy._comment: the mode copy: arrays laid out in a different order, then one serialisation buffer. Built by 0x141401060 (variant A) / 0x140afd660 (variant B), filled by 0x1414016b0. Every offset after the team array is encoded as a 32-bit field, so the copy can be re-laid-out in place; the team array is at +0x50 in a disp8 and therefore stays where it is, and everything after it moves instead.
copy._size_note: 0x141400b10 clamps the codec's serialised length against this constant and 0x141400ba0 returns it outright; both feed an allocator (0x140afbe06, 0x140af1baa).

_comment: Master League saves are written from mode copy A, which keeps its own copies of the
block's arrays at the caps its constructor hard-codes (copy.caps_from_ctor). Raising a
block cap without raising the copy's drops every record past the copy's cap from the
save, and the load fills the block back only up to it: the match table did that to the
schedule, the team, coach and regulation tables to the managed club, its manager and
its league. This part grows the copy's tables to the block's caps.
The copy is one flat object, so a table can only grow by moving everything above it.
Each region below is [base, base + cap_old * stride), verified to end exactly where the
next field begins; a field's shift is the sum of the growths of every region that starts
below it (prefix sum), and one patch per site carries the final value. The team array is
at +0x50 in a disp8 that cannot be widened, so it stays and everything above it moves.
teams drives two regions from one count (the records at +0x50 and a 0x10-byte per-team
side array at +0xc016b4, both counted by `mov ebp, 0x2ee` at 0x1414010b1), so both grow.
fixtures keeps its shipped 2000 in both block and copy: only its base moves.
fields is every copy A field tools/copyfields.py finds by following the copy pointer
through the six A functions (bounded to each function's own extent), plus the four only
reached from outside the copy code (attrib.json copy-manual). The generator re-runs that
walk and refuses if it finds a field this list does not have.
Not carried by the copy: matchflags. There is no 0x32c8 immediate in the A code outside
the three rec596 count sites, and no region of 13000 bytes anywhere in the field gaps.
Not grown here: competitions80 at +0x1049b3c, 80 records of 0x15fc. The block caps it at
80 as well (0x1414bc960: cmp edx, 0x50; records at block+0x1719b84), so it is a block
wall first and a copy wall second, and growing it is a relocation like rec596's.

variant_b._comment: The same allocation laid out a second way, built by 0x140afd660.  Every array is smaller than in variant A, so every offset after the coach array differs, and none of them is in the shift table that mlcopy uses for A.  Measured from the constructor on 2026-09-17: each `lea rbx, [rsi + off]` is followed by the record count in edi, the per-record constructor, and the stride the builder adds.
variant_b._packing_note: The fixture array is packed hard against rec596: 0x2a24c0 - 0x1c4210 == 0xde2b0 == 1750 * 0x208, to the byte.  Variant A is packed the same way, 0x329b00 - 0x22bc80 == 0xfde80 == 2000 * 0x208.  So doubling the fixture record leaves no slack anywhere: rec596 and everything after it has to move, in both variants, and copy.size with it.
variant_b._sites_note: Every site in the image that names one of variant B's offsets, from `copyscan.py --variant b`.  Thirty-one of them, in four runs: the constructor 0x140afd660 (11), two near-identical walkers around 0x1413fead7 and 0x1413feeaf (17), and three strays.  Coaches is not searched for, because 0x133a30 is shared with variant A and a hit on it says nothing about which layout the site belongs to.
